A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of broiler chickens can be maintained with Seq of 1 protein-rich and 1 energy-rich feed, but the performance is better if the protein difference is moderate.
Seq feeding is feasible for broiler chickens, and that the effects of protein and energy imbalance are dependent on their magnitude and on the length of the feeding period.
Seq of 2 feeds with a moderate protein difference and 48-h cycles are suitable to be used in practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is feasible to feed broilers on a sequential basis, but the results of the studies are not clear on how to do this to maximize growth and feed conversion.
the 48-h-cycle of Seq is a promising approach for broiler production.
it is possible to use Seq feeding to reduce the protein and energy content of the diet, which can result in lower cost and reduced environmental impact of poultry production.
